home.title: {brand} · Notifications that fit your day
home.desc: An Android app that holds the notifications you choose and delivers them together at the times you set. No internet permission; everything stays on your phone. In closed testing on Google Play.
home.lead: It holds the notifications you choose and delivers them together at times you set, such as 12:30, 18:00 and 21:00. Calls, alarms and the apps you mark as important always come through right away.
home.demo_h: Watch one day pass in a minute.
home.demo_p: The ring is a 24-hour plan, just like in the app. As the clock moves, the active mode changes, and each incoming notification is shown right away, held until the next delivery time, or blocked. At each delivery time, everything waiting arrives together.
home.demo_fine: An animation with example rules and example app types. Everything is generated in your browser; it is not real usage data.
home.how_h: One choice per app. The app does the rest.
home.how_p: Pick one of four options for each app. Set delivery times that fit your day, then choose a mode or let the weekly plan switch modes for you.

actions.p: The notification waits quietly while the chosen mode is on.
Collected and delivered together at the times you choose (for example 12:30, 18:00, 21:00).
Notifications from this app are not shown.

home.never_p: Calls, alarms, reminders, calendar and navigation notifications always come through. You can add apps such as your bank or hospital app to the Never hold list; they come through in every mode. If you like, you get one more reminder when one of their notifications is not opened within five minutes.

never_list.t: Apps on your Never hold list

home.modes_h: Four calm modes. Make your own if you like.

modes.p: Notifications without a rule arrive right away. Your per-app choices still apply.
Holds the apps that pull you away while you study or work.
A quiet night. What matters still comes through.
Holds only the sports apps you choose, so you don't learn the score before you watch the match.

highlights.p: Modes switch on their own by day and time. You can also set a plan for one specific date.
A repeating cycle of morning, evening and night shifts and days off, with breaks inside a shift.
Save a coupon, bill or expense notification to a folder when you choose to. You get one reminder on the morning of the due date.
Protect the whole app, or only the archive and notification contents, with Android's own lock screen prompt.
The whole day in one ring on the Today screen. A waiting notification shows the app and the reason, not the message.
For each mode, see which apps arrive right away and which wait, and why. Change it with one tap.

home.priv_h: Your notifications stay on your phone.
home.priv_p: The app has no internet permission. Nothing is sent over a network, and there are no ads or analytics tools.

facts.p: Network connections. The app does not ask for internet permission.

Things used to decide whether to hold a notification: the app, the notification type and the time. If Show notification content is on, the text is also checked on your phone to recognise important notifications such as order updates and bank transactions. When it is off, content is not read. Spoiler words are also checked on your phone only when you turn on spoiler mode.
How long content is kept is your choice. Notification content is shown in the app and stays encrypted on your phone; you choose how long it's kept, or turn it off completely in Settings.

home.priv_more_p: Settings and records are kept encrypted on your phone. Notification content is shown in the app and kept for as long as you choose, and bank payments, coupons, spending and bills go into the automatic archive. All of this can be turned off in Settings, and it only leaves your phone if you export it to a file. Uninstalling the app deletes its data.
home.status_h: In closed testing on Google Play.
home.status_p: The app runs on Android 8 and later. During closed testing (until 31 January 2027) every feature is free. To join the test, send the email address of your Google account to {email}; we'll add you to the tester list and send you the link to join.

features.title: Features · {brand}
features.desc: Everything the app can do today: per-app rules, delivery times, modes, weekly plan, shift schedule, notification archive and fingerprint lock. No internet permission.
features.lead: This page lists only what is in the current development build. New items from the latest update are marked.

items.p: Immediately, hold, at delivery time or block. Rules can also apply to an app group or a category.
Set several delivery times a day, such as 12:30, 18:00 and 21:00. Everything waiting arrives together.
Apps you add here come through in every mode. Optionally, get one more reminder if a notification is not opened within five minutes.
Calls, missed calls, alarms, reminders, calendar and navigation notifications are never held.

One silent line in the notification bar, with no sound or vibration, shows who has how many notifications waiting and when the first one will arrive. Content is not shown. Turn it on for the apps you choose or for everything that waits. A “Deliver now” button gives you everything waiting at once, without opening the app.
Normal, Focus, Sleep and Sports. Rename them, hide the ones you don't use, or create your own modes.
For each mode, see which apps arrive right away and which wait, with the reason. Add an app, group or category to say “this one comes through in this mode”.

Modes switch by day and time. Browse months and years, see how many notifications arrived, waited and were delivered on a past day (counts only), and set a plan for a future date. Date-specific plans are listed with their dates. While editing a plan, pick weekdays or the weekend with one tap. Tap a day in the calendar to see its modes and delivery times and switch them on or off.
The Today screen shows the whole day on one ring with the waiting notifications. A countdown shows when the next delivery comes, for example “5 notifications in 38 min”.
A repeating cycle of morning, evening and night shifts and days off. Breaks inside a shift are applied too.
Preview what a profile changes before you apply it, and edit it. A profile lasts as long as its name says (for example “Deep work · 2 hours”) and then returns to the previous mode.
Tap “Focus for 25 min” on the Today screen. When time is up, you go back to your previous mode and see a short “well done” summary (counts only).

While you watch a match, the sports, news and social apps you choose wait until it ends, then everything arrives together. Optionally add team names or spoiler words; with content access on, they are matched only on your phone.
See which apps a rule such as “Shopping” covers. Remove an app that was guessed wrong, or add a new one.
Put apps into groups and manage them with one rule. Rename a group or change its apps at any time.
The Rules screen lists every app on your phone, not only the ones that have already sent a notification.
With your permission, the app can switch modes during calendar meetings or when your phone connects to your car over Bluetooth.
Save your rules to a file and restore them later. The backup also keeps mode names, hidden modes and each mode's list of apps that come through right away.

Setup starts by getting to know your phone: your apps are sorted into groups, and you fix any that land in the wrong one. You are only asked about groups you actually have, and at the end you see a preview of who comes through and who waits. Choose “Start simple” and setup ends in 3 steps with the simple view turned on.
The Today screen lists the apps without a rule that interrupted you most this week. Move one to delivery time with a single tap, or choose “Not now”. Only counts are used.

Turn it on in Settings: the Today screen keeps only the dial, a single “Focus / Back to normal” button and the waiting notifications. The Rules and Plan tabs are hidden, and your rules keep working in the background. For people who want to use the app with as few settings as possible.
In History, every held notification shows which mode or rule held it. From there you can also move that app to delivery time without opening the rules screen.
Once in the morning, the app asks about the app without a rule that interrupted you most yesterday. Hold it with a single tap.

Normal when you get home, Focus when you arrive at work. You set it up with your phone's routines app (on Samsung, “Modes and Routines”); ha!shh does not ask for location permission. Settings → Mode by Wi-Fi shows the steps. Home screen shortcuts and routines switch the mode without opening the app; only a short message appears.

Treat the notification types of one app differently: for example, Instagram messages right away, likes and comments at delivery time. The types are learned from what the app reports, with no content analysis. Ready shortcuts such as “Messages only” set it up with one tap.

Save any notification into folders like Coupons, Bills to pay or Spending, or into a folder of your own. The app suggests the amount and you confirm it; a monthly total is shown. Give it a due date and you're reminded that morning; you can also add it to your phone's calendar (no calendar permission needed). Bank payments, coupons, spending and bills go into the archive automatically as soon as they arrive; you can turn this, or any of these types, off in Settings.

Protect the whole app, or only the archive and notification contents, with your fingerprint, face or phone PIN. Android's own prompt is used, so your fingerprint data never reaches the app. In the “archive and contents” setting, content previews in History also stay hidden until you unlock.

items.t: Content stays on your phone, under your control
items.p: The content of waiting and past notifications is shown in the app and kept encrypted on your phone; you choose how long it's kept. If you'd rather not, turn off content display in Settings; then only the app name, time and reason for waiting are shown.

Choose Paper (warm cream, the default), Light (white), Dark or System, which uses Paper in light mode and Dark in dark mode. When you change the theme, the app asks whether to match the home screen icon too. On Android 13 and later, themed icons take your wallpaper color. Night and Day themes are available too.
From Settings, your email app opens with a ready message. Adding device information is optional.
Group your archive by app, person or a word you write. Each group shows a counter and its latest notifications; notifications you mark as read that match a group go into it.

In an archive folder you choose, spending from bank notifications adds up (refunds and cancellations are subtracted), and coupon codes gather in one list with their expiry dates. Copy a code with one tap. Kept encrypted on your phone.

Save your archive as a password-protected or a plain file to Google Drive, Dropbox or your phone, and restore it on a new phone with one tap. The app never goes online; your phone's own file picker does the saving.

Every installation has a random invite code. When a friend joins and sends you their thank-you code, you unlock badges and wallpapers (rewards are only visual). Works without internet; nobody learns who you are.

features.tech_p: These describe the current development build (0.89). Numbers come from the source code.

tech.v: Java 17 and the Android SDK only; no third-party libraries
31 core logic test files; the build stops if any test fails
A notification listener and Android's own snooze, so the original notification comes back on time instead of being copied
No internet permission; no servers, accounts, ads or analytics
Encrypted on the phone with a key kept in the Android Keystore
Tested on a Samsung Galaxy S24 and an Android 15 emulator; in closed testing on Google Play
Claude Code is the main development tool. The app itself contains no AI service.

privacy.title: Privacy policy · {brand}
privacy.desc: How the notification app handles data: no internet permission, everything stays encrypted on your phone; content display, retention and the automatic archive are under your control.
privacy.intro: In short: the app has no internet permission and sends nothing anywhere. Everything it keeps stays encrypted on your phone, and only you see it. Notification content is shown in the app and kept for as long as you choose, and bank payments, coupons, spending and bills go into the automatic archive. You can turn all of this off in Settings.

sections.body: The app is developed by Seçkin Çelik in Karabük, Türkiye. Contact: {email}.

The app needs the notification access you grant in Android settings. To decide whether a notification comes through right away or waits, it uses the app that sent it, the notification type (e.g. call, alarm or message category) and the time. If Show notification content is on, it also checks the text on your phone to recognise important notifications such as order updates and bank transactions. When it is off, content is not read. If you turn on spoiler mode, the words you chose (such as a team name) are also looked for in the notification's title and text, on your phone. Where else content is used is described in the sections below. Nothing is sent anywhere.

• Showing it (with your consent): If you tap “Accept and continue” during setup, the title and text of waiting and past notifications are shown to you in the app and the widget. If you don't consent, or you turn off Show notification content in Settings, content isn't read or kept; only the app name, time and reason for waiting are shown. While the app lock is on, the widget shows no text.
  • How long it's kept (30 days by default): History and content are kept encrypted on your phone for 30 days. In Settings you can choose 7, 90 or 365 days, or turn automatic deletion off. This time-based cleanup doesn't affect the archive. If you turn off showing content, stored content is deleted, including notification text in the archive.
  • Your own words: If you add spoiler words or archive word groups, the title and text are compared with those words on your phone.
  • Notification type filter: So you can recognise the types, one sample title per notification type of an app is kept encrypted on your phone.
  • History log: For every notification your phone receives, the app, the time and what happened (came through, held, delivered, marked as read) are kept in History on your phone.

• Automatic archive (on by default): Bank payments, coupons, spending and bills are saved to the archive as soon as they arrive. To recognise them, the title and text are compared on your phone with certain phrases (e.g. “payment made”, “due date”, a coupon code); nothing leaves your phone for this. You can turn the automatic archive, or any of its types, off in Settings. Automatic entries are kept for 365 days by default; you can choose the period, and entries you edit or add a note to are not deleted. If you turn off content display, the automatic archive stops too.
  • Apart from that, the archive holds the notifications you choose to archive and, if you have set up archive groups, notifications you marked as read that match one of your groups: app name, title, text and date, plus the folder, amount and due date you added. These stay encrypted on your phone until you delete them.
  • Spending totals and coupon lists are calculated on your phone from your archived notifications. Copying a coupon code puts it on your phone's clipboard.
  • The suggested amount is calculated on your phone. Due-date reminders are set with your phone's own alarm.
  • Adding an archive entry to your calendar opens your own calendar app with a pre-filled event: the notification's title (or the app name if there is no title) is suggested as the event name and the due date (all day) as the date. You see the event there, can change it, and choose whether to save it. The app does not ask for calendar permission for this. If your calendar syncs with an account (such as Google), the event you save goes to that account too; your calendar app does that, ha!shh sends nothing.
  • You can export the archive with your phone's own file picker to a place you choose (such as Google Drive, Dropbox or a folder on your phone): either as a file protected with a strong password, or as an unencrypted file anyone who has it can read. If you turned off content display, the title and text are left empty in the file. Where the file goes and who can open it then depends on you and the service you chose; ha!shh itself sends nothing.
The lock uses Android's own biometric prompt. Your fingerprint or face data never reaches the app; the app only learns whether unlocking succeeded.

• Posting notifications: to deliver held notifications and reminders to you.
  • Starting at boot: to set your rules and reminders up again after your phone restarts.
  • Vibration: So held notifications make no sound, ha!shh manages notification sounds and plays the sound and vibration of notifications that come through right away itself. Calls and alarms are not affected; this can be turned off in Settings.
  • Keeping awake: So the decision about a notification that arrives while the screen is off isn't delayed, the phone is kept awake for at most 3 seconds.
  • Calendar (optional): to change mode during meetings, only the start and end times and busy status of events are read. Event titles are not read.
  • Bluetooth (optional): to change mode when your phone connects to your car. The device's raw address is not stored; only an irreversible fingerprint and the device name you see are kept, encrypted.
  • Exact alarms: so modes start and end right on time. If this is off, changes may run slightly late.

To sort your apps into groups and show them in the rule lists, the app reads the list of installed apps that appear on your home screen (app name, package name and the type Android reports). This happens only on the phone and uses no extra permission. The quiet summary is the app's own silent notification; it shows only app names and counts, never notification content.
The app has no internet permission. There are no servers, accounts, ads, analytics or crash reporting tools. No data from the app reaches the developer or anyone else.

If you buy a subscription, the payment and the subscription are handled by Google Play, and Google processes the purchase information under its own privacy policy. The app only learns from the Play Store app on your phone whether you have an active subscription; it does not use its own internet connection for this and does not see your payment details. Promo codes are redeemed in the Play Store; the app does not store the code.

Each installation creates a random invite code on the phone; it contains no personal information. If you invite someone, you choose the app to share it with; the shared Google Play link contains only this code. Your friend's app creates a thank-you code, which they send to you themselves, and your counter goes up on your phone. No server is involved and the app does not learn who you invited. Rewards are only badges and wallpapers.

If you use Send feedback in Settings, your own email app opens with a prepared message. You write and send it yourself. Device information (manufacturer, model, Android version, app version) is added only if you tick that option. The email travels through your email provider. Notification content and your rules are never added. If you send the message, the developer sees your email address and uses it only to reply to you. Messages received at {email} are used only to reply to you and improve the app, and are not shared with third parties.

The website ha-shh.com has no ads, cookies or third-party trackers. To count visits it uses its own cookieless counter: only daily totals are kept on this site's server (number of visits, which pages were opened, clicks on the email link and the website a visit came from, such as google). No IP address, cookie or device ID is saved; your browser only keeps “counted today” and “visited before” marks for itself. The help assistant answers from the texts on this site, inside your browser. Read-aloud runs on your device. Voice input uses your browser's own speech service; some browsers (such as Chrome) process the audio on their servers. If you choose to send a conversation, only its questions and answers and your optional note are saved, with the date, the page and whether you used a phone or a computer. No name, email address or IP address is saved. Conversations are kept for at most 12 months and are used only to improve the app and the assistant. To have yours deleted, write to {email} with the date and time.

You can save a backup of your rules and modes as a file. It includes mode names, hidden built-in modes and, for each mode, the apps, groups and categories that come through right away. You can also export your notification records (app, time and what was done). Neither of these files contains notification content. The archive has its own export, described above. Files go only to the app or folder you select. Android cloud backup is turned off for this app. If you share a notification, its title and text go to the app you choose in Android's share sheet.

Settings → Privacy and data → Delete all my local data permanently deletes all of the app's data on your phone, photos included. Uninstalling the app does the same. You can also delete archive entries and history one by one.
If the app changes how it handles data, this page will be updated and the date at the top will change.

faq.title: FAQ and support · {brand}
faq.desc: Answers to common questions about the notification app: privacy, battery, supported phones, the archive and how to send feedback.
faq.lead: Short answers to the questions we hear most. If yours is not here, send an email.

items.q: When will the app be available?
items.a: It's in closed testing on Google Play. During the test (until 31 January 2027) every feature is free. To join, send the email address of your Google account to {email}; we'll add you to the list and send you the link to join. The public release date will be set when closed testing ends.

After a 3-day free trial, ha!shh is a yearly subscription: US $9.99 or ₺179.99 a year (in other countries, Google Play shows the local price). Without a subscription, the app keeps working in a passive mode: it holds nothing, but still counts and groups your notifications and shows how often you were interrupted today. At launch, the first 1,000 users get 6 months free with a promo code. No ads and no data sales.

items.q: Does the app read my notifications?
items.a: We don't: the app has no internet permission and nothing leaves your phone. The app decides whether to hold a notification using the app, the notification type and the time (if you turn on spoiler mode, the words you chose are looked for too). Content is read on your phone to show it to you, to keep it for as long as you choose, and to archive bank payments, coupons, spending and bills automatically. If you'd rather not, turn off Show notification content in Settings.

items.q: Could I miss an important call or message?
items.a: Calls, alarms, reminders, calendar and navigation notifications are never held. Apps on your Never hold list come through in every mode, and the app can remind you once more if such a notification is not opened within five minutes.

items.q: Why does it have no internet permission?
items.a: It does not need one. Everything happens on your phone, so your notifications cannot be sent anywhere.

It does not run a constant background service or keep checking in a loop. It reacts to notifications through Android's notification listener and uses the phone's alarms for delivery times. Some manufacturers limit background apps; the setup screens show how to allow it on your phone.

items.q: Which phones does it work on?
items.a: Android 8 and later. The fingerprint lock needs Android 9 or later and a screen lock (fingerprint, PIN or pattern) set up on the phone.

items.q: Do notifications go into the archive on their own?
items.a: Bank payments, coupons, spending and bills, yes: the automatic archive is on by default and saves them as soon as they arrive. Other notifications are saved only if you archive them or they match an archive group you set up. You can turn the automatic archive, or any of its types, off in Settings. The archive stays encrypted on your phone and only leaves it if you export it to a file. You can add a folder, amount and due date, and delete entries whenever you like.

items.q: What happens if I uninstall the app?
items.a: All of its data is deleted from the phone. Android cloud backup is off, so if you want to keep your rules, export them to a file first.
The app is being prepared in English, Turkish, Arabic, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Indonesian, Portuguese and Russian. During development, some new screens appear in Turkish first.

items.q: How do I report a problem or suggest an idea?
items.a: In the app, open Settings and choose Send feedback; your email app opens with a ready message. You can also write directly to {email}.

updates.title: Updates · {brand}
updates.desc: What's new in ha!shh: new features and fixes in the Google Play closed-testing version.
updates.lead: What's new in ha!shh. The app is in closed testing on Google Play; everything here is in the test version and will be in the public release too.

items: Closed testing: ha!shh is in closed testing on Google Play. During the test (until 31 January 2027) every feature is unlocked and no subscription is asked for. To join, send the email address of your Google account to {email}.

Tap the widget: In Dial and Pool, what's waiting opens: a list at wide sizes, a card at small sizes; after 10 seconds or one tap the widget returns to normal. In Deck, tapping anywhere on the card opens the notification panel.
Share from the widget: From a notification's menu you can send its content to an app you choose.

Show now is more reliable: If the app removed its notification, ha!shh shows a copy; a notification doesn't arrive twice, and one you marked as read doesn't come back. If ha!shh's own notifications are off, a short warning appears.

Tidier screens: Waiting lists show the arrival time, newest on top. Layout on small widgets is fixed, and Classic shows more rows at the large size. The screen stays on in desk view. The quick settings tile really changes the mode.
Privacy: When you turn off content access, stored titles of waiting notifications are deleted right away too.

Fixes: The app no longer closes when you change the icon along with the theme; it doesn't freeze when many notifications arrive at once; a language chosen in the app applies right away, offline and on older Android versions; all text is in 10 languages.

news.h: New widget styles and Work Schedule
items: Four widget styles: Classic, Dial, Deck and Pool. Pick one in Settings; what you can do stays the same. Small sizes (2x2, 4x1) look right too.

The widget, your way: The newest notification sits on top, or put the oldest first if you prefer; a Yesterday heading and dates for older days appear. You can hide one app's content in the widget: the row stays, the text doesn't show. With nothing waiting, it can show an emoji or your own photo.
Work Schedule: Set up your fixed or shift schedule on one card; setup uses the same schedule.

Delay in every mode: You can delay an app's notifications by the minutes you choose in every mode (e.g. live scores). At delivery, ha!shh can show its own alert with sound. Calls, alarms and permanent blocks aren't affected.
Share a notification: If content access is on, you can share a notification's title and text with an app you choose.
Clear consent: Notification content is only read and shown if you tap “Accept and continue” during setup. Tap “Not now” and the app works with just the app name, notification type and time.

Fixes: Less hold delay when notifications arrive in a burst; marking many as read no longer freezes the app; if notification access drops, the app tries to reconnect; scrolling the Feed no longer refreshes the page or loses Undo; Undo works on the last card; keeping the screen on in desk view, including on battery, can be set in Settings.

news.h: Four-question setup, Just arrived and simpler screens
items: Four-question setup: When you don't want to be disturbed, who should always reach you, how you want to see the rest, and what may wake you at night. Your answers set up modes, delivery, important notifications and sleep exceptions together.

All-day focus: During setup you can pick a focus profile with no end time: only calls and the important notifications you choose come through right away; the rest waits in the home screen widget. On the Today screen you can also keep Focus on “Until I turn it off”.

Just arrived on the desk calendar: With the phone sideways, notifications that came through without being held (e.g. messages) show as small icons for the last hour; tap one to go to the notification. Notification content isn't shown.

Preview card on the desk calendar: Tap the icon of an app with waiting notifications and a small card opens listing what's waiting from that app; a second tap opens the notification. The card doesn't cover the clock, and no text is shown if content access is off.
App breakdown in the delivery summary: In History → Delivery summary, tap a category to see how many notifications came from which app.

Order status recognition: If content access is on, statuses like “out for delivery”, “courier on the way” and “delivered” are recognised in 14 languages in shopping and food apps; ads are not. With access off, the text isn't read.

Worldwide: Common banking, shopping and delivery apps in the US, Canada, the UK, Germany, Spain, the Netherlands, Scandinavia, Japan, South Korea and Australia go into the right group. All times follow your phone's 12/24-hour setting.

Simpler screens: Rules has a single “Add rule” button and a three-step rule wizard. Settings shows seven essentials first, with the rest under “More”. The Work, School, Meeting, Holiday and Driving modes are hidden for now; plans you made with them keep working.
Permanent block always wins: An app or type you've permanently silenced stays silent even if it's on the “always deliver” list.

Fixes: Opening a notification from History works again on Android 14 and later (e.g. Gmail); a new WhatsApp message in the same chat now plays a sound; no empty group row is left in the notification shade; scrolling in the Feed no longer makes the screen jump; panels don't cover the clock in landscape; on the desk calendar, brightness is only dimmed if “Low-power desk view” is selected; delivery times you deleted don't come back.

The app in 10 languages: Every screen is available in English, Turkish, Arabic, German, Spanish, French, Hindi, Indonesian, Portuguese and Russian. You can also pick the language inside the app, in Settings → Appearance.

Home screen widgets: In four sizes, showing the next delivery, the active mode, how many are waiting and the apps with the most waiting. The large size lists waiting notifications, and one tap marks them as read. Widgets follow your theme; tap the time to see the current time.

Desk view: Turn your phone sideways for a big clock, the active mode, a week strip, the next delivery and what's waiting. Choose what to show, and use your own photo as a frame or background. The screen stays on while charging; in low-power layout it dims and refreshes once a minute.

Every notification in History: Notifications that came through right away now go into History too, so you can find one you dismissed by mistake. You choose during setup how long History is kept; if you don't, nothing is deleted automatically, and if it takes up space you're asked before anything is cleared.

Automatic archive: Bank payments, coupons, completed spending and bills go into the archive as soon as they arrive; prices in ads don't. Entries you added or edited yourself always stay. It can be turned off; amounts are shown in your phone's currency.
Quiet waiting: Held notifications make no sound at all; ha!shh plays the sound of the ones that come through right away. Calls and alarms are not affected.
Undo: When you swipe a waiting card to mark it as read or snooze it, you can undo within 4 seconds.

Simpler screens: Rules, Plan and History were reorganised; the notification report and statistics are on one screen. First-time setup also sets up a night Sleep plan. Blocking screenshots on sensitive screens is now an option you turn on in Settings.

Fixes: The delay in holding notifications while the screen is off is fixed; notifications that arrive silently follow your rules too; Android system and SIM notifications are never held; when a mode ends, everything it held arrives together; on daylight-saving nights modes end at the right time; shopping apps land in the right group; other apps can't open or change ha!shh's screens and theme.

Invite and earn rewards: every installation has a random invite code. Share it with the app you choose; when a friend installs ha!shh and enters it, their app gives them a thank-you code to send back to you, and your counter goes up.
Rewards are just for fun: 1 invite unlocks the “First invite” badge, 3 the Paper wallpaper, 5 the “Quiet circle” badge, 7 the Night wallpaper and 10 the “ha!shh ambassador” badge.
No server, no tracking: invites work without internet; nobody learns who you are.

Also new: a two-column layout when the phone is on its side, an automatic simple view when battery saver is on, app icons in the expanded quiet summary, live notifications (such as order tracking) kept with their latest progress in History, a larger time picker and an Archive button at the top of History.

news.h: Spoiler mode, archive wallet and backup to your own cloud
items: Spoiler mode: while you watch a match, notifications from the sports, news and social apps you choose wait until it ends, then arrive together. You can add team names or spoiler words; with content access on, they are matched only on your phone.

Spending total and coupon wallet: in an archive folder you choose, spending from bank notifications adds up (refunds and cancellations are subtracted), and coupon codes gather in one list with their expiry dates, ready to copy with one tap.
Archive groups: group your archive by app, person or a word you write. Notifications you mark as read that match a group go into it.

Take your archive with you: save it as a password-protected or a plain file to Google Drive, Dropbox or your phone, and restore it on a new phone. The app itself still never goes online; your phone's own file picker does the saving.
Notification type filter: for example, Instagram messages arrive right away while likes and comments wait for delivery time. It uses the notification types the app reports, not the message text.
Calendar day details: tap a day to see its modes and delivery times and switch them on or off.
Smoother everyday use: swiping cards away no longer stutters, tapping a notification opens it in its app, setup continues where you left off, and duplicate “ghost” notifications are gone.
Launch offer: at launch, the first 1,000 users will get 6 months free with a code you redeem in Google Play.
Coming soon: new Night and Day themes with a 3D dial.

news.h: Archive, fingerprint lock and a calmer start
items: Notification archive with folders, amounts and due-date reminders.
Fingerprint lock for the whole app, or only for the archive and notification contents.
Who comes through, who waits: see it for every mode, plus a weekly clean-up suggestion.
Quiet summary, focus session, simple view and smart setup.
Paper theme and new app icons.

news.h: Shift schedules, a Never hold list and fairer rules
items: Shift schedule: a repeating cycle of morning, evening and night shifts and days off.
Never hold list: chosen apps come through in every mode, with an optional reminder if a notification is not opened within five minutes.
Newly installed apps ask which group they belong to.

Fairer by design: the app no longer guesses from message text, so other apps cannot jump the queue by writing “urgent”. Reminders always come through, and Sleep and Focus take priority over other rules.
Safer: other apps can no longer switch your mode without your permission.
A calm summary of the time you kept, with no streaks or goals, and a Today screen that updates live.

news.h: Quick mode buttons and match protection
items: Quick mode buttons to switch modes with one tap.
Timed match protection: chosen sports apps wait until the match is over, so you don't learn the score early.
Home screen shortcuts for modes.
Battery guidance during setup for phone brands that stop apps in the background.

news.h: The beginning: what the first builds could do
items: By 3 October 2026, the first development builds already had the core of ha!shh:
One choice per app: immediately, hold, at delivery time or block.
Delivery times such as 12:30, 18:00 and 21:00, where everything waiting arrives together.
Modes and a weekly plan on a 24-hour dial, plus “pause for today” and “hold this app until tomorrow”.
Calm for notification storms: an app that sends many notifications in a row is quietened for a while.
Optional automations for calendar meetings and your car's Bluetooth, a Quick Settings tile and a backup file for your rules.
Privacy from day one: no internet permission and encrypted storage on the phone.
On 3 October came the first setup wizard, search in waiting notifications and History, and preparation for 10 languages.

setup.t: How do I set it up?
setup.a: ha!shh is in closed testing on Google Play; once you join the test you install it from the Play Store (to join, write to {email}). On first launch it asks for notification access and for your consent to show notification content. Then come four questions: when you don't want to be disturbed, who should always reach you, how you want to see the rest, and what may wake you at night. You can change delivery times whenever you like.

terms.title: Terms of use · {brand}
terms.desc: Terms of use and subscription for the ha!shh Android app: Google Play subscription, trial, cancellation, test period and liability.
terms.intro: In short: you use ha!shh on your own phone, with your own rules. Subscription and payment go through Google Play, and you cancel there too. The app holds notifications according to your settings; you decide who comes through right away so you don't miss anything important.

sections.body: These terms apply to your use of the ha!shh Android app (package name com.hashh.app) and the ha-shh.com website. The app is developed by Seçkin Çelik in Karabük, Türkiye. Contact: {email}. By installing and using the app, you accept these terms.

ha!shh holds the notifications that arrive on your phone according to your rules and times, and shows them together when you choose. To do this it needs Android's notification access permission. How your data is handled is described on the Privacy policy page.

• ha!shh is used with a yearly subscription. Google Play handles purchase, payment and billing; the price for your country is shown in Google Play.
  • If Google Play offers you a free trial, the trial length and the amount due afterwards are shown before you buy. If you don't cancel before the trial ends, the paid subscription starts.
  • The subscription renews automatically every year until you cancel. You can cancel at any time in Google Play → Payments & subscriptions; you keep access until the end of the period you've paid for.
  • Promo codes are redeemed in Google Play.
Refund requests are made through Google Play under Google Play's refund rules. Your rights under the consumer law of the country you live in are not affected.

If no subscription is active, the app runs in passive mode: it holds no notifications and they arrive right away. Your rules stay on your phone; when you subscribe again, you carry on where you left off.

The app is currently in closed testing on Google Play. During the test (until 31 January 2027) every feature is free and no subscription is required. Test versions may have bugs; if you find any, write to {email} and we'll fix them. After the test period a subscription is needed to continue; you'll be told in advance in the app and on this site.

• You decide which notifications come through right away and which wait. Calls and alarms are never held; even so, it's up to you to add notifications that matter for work, health or safety to the “always deliver” list.
  • Don't use ha!shh as your only source of emergency, health or safety alerts.
  • Use the app lawfully and only on your own device; don't reverse-engineer, copy or redistribute it.

We develop and test the app carefully, but we can't guarantee it will work without interruptions or errors. Your Android version, your phone maker's battery-saving settings or turning off permissions can delay notifications or make them behave differently than expected. To the extent permitted by applicable law, we are not liable for indirect damage caused by a missed or delayed notification. This limitation does not affect liability for intent or gross negligence, or your statutory rights as a consumer.
The app, its name, its icon and the content of this site belong to the developer. A subscription gives you the right to use the app personally; it does not transfer the app itself.

If these terms change, this page is updated and the date at the top changes; we also announce important changes in the app. You can stop using the app at any time by uninstalling it; you need to cancel your subscription separately in Google Play.

These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of Türkiye. Mandatory consumer-protection rules of the country you live in still apply. If there's a problem, please write to {email} first and we'll try to sort it out together.
